An ancient fae-chapel cottage of tall uneven grey ashlar blocks laced with pale lichen, its steep single gable rising sharply against the treeline, three tall gothic arched windows glowing warm amber, heavy arched oak doors with black strap hinges set beneath a gabled stone porch, and a tiny moss-capped bell-cupola crowning the ridge.

A low long cottage of centuries-worn honey fieldstone in crooked courses, its sweeping ridgeline barely clearing the wildflowers, deep eaves shadowing three eyebrow dormers lit softly amber, a rounded silvered-plank door with an iron ring-pull, and a gabled stone porch whose lintel is entirely buried under a thick bolster of living moss.

An L-shaped cottage of pale weathered grey stone blocks, two rooflines meeting at a crooked angle, the shorter wing leaning into the longer like a tired companion, arched windows glowing honey-gold in both gables, a rounded oak door with black strap hinges, and a tall ivy-climbed chimney with a tiny rowan sapling sprouting from its crown.

A catslide-roofed cottage of uneven fieldstone furred green at every edge, its long mossy roof sweeping in one great slope nearly to the wildflowers on the downhill side, a single arched window glowing amber just above the eave-line, a rounded plank door with an iron ring-pull, and a stone bench worn smooth beside the threshold.

A turf-roofed burrow-cottage half-sunk into a flowering bank of clover and harebells, its curved round door of darkened oak with black iron strap hinges set flush with the hillside, two small arched windows glowing warm on either side, weathered fieldstone courses visible where the bank peels back, and a crown of ox-eye daisies rioting along the turf ridgeline.

A cottage grown around a living ancient beech, the great pale trunk braided through lichen-patched grey stone-block walls, one bough lifting the mossy twin-gabled roofline at a gentle angle, arched windows glowing amber between root and stone, a rounded silvered door with a hand-forged iron ring-pull set in the hollow where two roots divide.

A little gabled stone watermill cottage straddling a brook on mossy stone piers, its uneven grey blocks furred green at every course, a dark moss-slicked waterwheel turning slowly in the current below, small arched windows glowing warm amber over the water, and a rounded plank door with an iron ring-pull reached by a single worn stone footbridge.

An ancient fae-chapel cottage of tall lichen-crusted honey ashlar, its steep single gable sheeted in ivy from plinth to ridge-cap, two gothic arched windows glowing deep amber, an arched oak door with black strap hinges beneath a stone label-mould, and a tiny verdigris-balled finial at the gable peak catching pale filtered light through the canopy.

A long low cottage of pale grey fieldstone in uneven courses, its low sweeping ridgeline running nearly the width of a meadow clearing, deep eaves throwing cool shadow over three arched windows glowing gold, a rounded oak door with an iron ring-pull up two hollowed stone steps, and a slowly turning moss-slicked waterwheel on the brook at the gable end.

A stepped hillside cottage climbing a mossy bank on two levels, its lower storey of dark lichen-patched fieldstone half-buried in the slope, the upper storey of paler ashlar rising behind with a steeper gabled roof, arched windows glowing amber on both levels, a rounded plank door with black strap hinges on the lower face, and a tall ivy-climbed chimney crowning the upper gable.

A turf-roofed burrow-cottage pressed into a bank of wild thyme and foxglove, its perfectly round oak door with a hand-forged iron ring-pull centered between two deep-set arched windows glowing honey-warm, the stone courses of pale weathered fieldstone visible between root and earth, and a thick bolster of sedge and tiny ferns carpeting the living roof above.

A cottage grown around a living ancient yew, the dark furrowed trunk passing through the corner of lichen-crusted stone-block walls, mossy gabled roof lifted unevenly by a reaching bough, two arched windows glowing amber flanking the trunk, a rounded silvered-plank door with black iron strap hinges, and a tiny iron weathervane at the gable tip, green with age.

A twin-gabled cottage of uneven honey fieldstone, two steep rooflines intersecting at a crooked ridge, both gables capped in deep moss with tiny ferns threading the verge, arched windows glowing warm amber in each face, a rounded oak door with an iron ring-pull beneath a gabled stone porch, and ivy sheeting the shorter gable entirely from sill to ridge.

A catslide-roofed cottage of centuries-worn pale grey ashlar, the great mossy roof beginning at the full ridge height and sweeping in one long plane almost to the ground on the north side, a single gothic arched window glowing amber just clearing the eave, a rounded plank door with black iron strap hinges on the high south face, and a stone bench half-sunk in wildflowers beside it.

An ancient fae-chapel cottage of tall uneven grey stone blocks patched with pale gold lichen, its steep single gable rising clean against the forest, a tall ivy-climbed chimney tower at one end, three gothic arched windows glowing amber, heavy arched oak doors with black strap hinges, and a tiny moss-capped bell-cupola set just behind the ridge on a short square neck of stone.

A round stone turret-cottage of rough lichen-crusted fieldstone, its single cylindrical tower topped by a moss-greened conical roof, one gothic arched window glowing amber facing the clearing, a rounded oak door with a hand-forged iron ring-pull, a lean-to addition of the same grey stone pressed against the curved wall, and a tiny iron weathervane spinning slowly at the conical peak.

A little gabled stone well-house cottage of pale weathered ashlar blocks, its steep single gable mossy and fern-trimmed, the ancient stone-coped well set inside under a small arched opening glowing amber-lit by a single arched window above, a rounded plank door with black strap hinges on iron pintles, and a weathered verdigris ball finial at the gable tip.

A turf-roofed burrow-cottage built into a south-facing bank of heather and clover, its round door of darkened silvered oak with a hand-forged ring-pull flanked by two arched windows glowing honey-warm, pale fieldstone courses visible between the earthen banks on either side, and a long green turf roof rolling overhead like a sleeping hillside, dotted with self-seeded harebells.

An L-shaped cottage of uneven grey fieldstone in crooked courses, the longer wing low and deep-eaved, the shorter wing rising to a steeper gabled roof at a slight angle, ivy sheeting the join between them, arched windows glowing amber in both wings, a rounded oak door with an iron ring-pull at the inner corner where the two wings meet, sheltered by their joined eaves.

A low long cottage of pale honey fieldstone, its deep eaves almost touching the wildflower bank on the uphill side, three eyebrow dormers pushing through the moss-capped ridgeline each with a tiny arched window glowing amber, a rounded plank door with black strap hinges at the centre, and a tall stone chimney so heavily ivy-climbed that only its cap of weathered stone shows through.

A cottage grown around a living ancient ash, the pale furrowed trunk rising through a deliberate gap in the lichen-patched grey stone-block wall, the mossy single gable tilting gently where a low bough rests on the purlin, arched windows glowing warm amber on either side of the trunk, and a rounded oak door with a hand-forged iron ring-pull set between two braided surface roots.

An ancient fae-chapel cottage of tall weathered honey ashlar with pale lichen freckling every block, its steep single gable and tall ivy-climbed chimney tower rising together against dark pines, two pairs of gothic arched windows glowing deep amber, an arched oak door with black strap hinges under a stone label-mould, and a tiny moss-capped bell-cupola on a short stone neck at the ridge shoulder.

A two-level stepped cottage of dark lichen-patched fieldstone climbing a mossy hillside, the lower level half-buried in the bank with a rounded plank door and iron ring-pull, the upper level reached by worn stone steps cut into the slope, its steeper gabled roof capped in thick moss, a single gothic arched window glowing amber on each level, and a tall chimney with a tiny fern sprouting from the crown.

A second little gabled stone watermill cottage straddling a narrow brook, its pale weathered fieldstone courses furred with moss at every horizontal edge, the dark waterwheel turning slowly on its iron axle below an arched stone tailrace, two arched windows glowing amber on the gabled end above the water, and a rounded silvered-plank door with black iron strap hinges on the dry bank face.

An ancient fae-chapel cottage of uneven pale grey ashlar blocks laced with gold and grey lichen, its steep single gable clean and graceful, deep-set gothic arched windows glowing warm amber behind their iron glazing bars, heavy arched oak double doors with black strap hinges set in a recessed stone arch, and a tiny moss-capped bell-cupola on a slender stone neck against the open sky.
